title: OpenAI's coding agents now log 3.1 workdays of effort per human workday
description:
OpenAI just published internal counts showing coding agents log 3.1 workdays of effort for every one human workday inside its research organization, with total agent runtime passing human labor time sometime after May. The company's median researcher went from light agent use early this year to more than $600 a day in inference by mid-August, while the top 10% of research users run more than $7,000 a day in tokens.
The number worth sitting with is the one about people: more than half of the successful four-to-eight-hour agent tasks still required a human to step in. That is a research role being redefined rather than removed, with judgment moving toward choosing which questions deserve the compute and deciding what the results actually mean. OpenAI is releasing these figures while preparing a stock flotation after a round valued it near $850 billion, so read them as a company's account of itself. They are also the first hard numbers outsiders can use to hold the lab to the pace it claims, which is exactly how verification starts catching up to capability.
